_comment: Catalog of stock Apple iPod firmware for `flashpod flash`. When no --firmware is given, flashpod offers this list, downloads the chosen image from base_url + file, caches it under ~/.cache/flashpod, and verifies it against sha256. The images are NOT bundled with flashpod (they are Apple's copyright); they are hosted as GitHub release assets. You can always bring your own with `--firmware <file>` (no network). Images ship as .bin.gz -- a gzipped raw Firmware-* image; load_firmware() dispatches on magic bytes, so a raw image or an Apple .ipsw works too if you supply one yourself. Apple ipsw naming was iPod_<family>.<version>.ipsw (family 1 = 1G/2G, 2 = 3G, 4/10 = 4G grayscale, 5 = photo, 11 = color); asset names keep that scheme and append the build date where it is known. build_date is recorded here so the picker need not parse images at runtime, but it IS recoverable from the bytes: these binaries carry their compiled-in C __DATE__ string ('Nov 01 2001'), which scripts/extract_firmware.py reads. That method is self-verifying -- it reproduces the dates already recorded for 0.0, 0.4, 1.4 and 1.5, two of which were established long before the script existed and have no zip timestamp they could have come from. DO NOT use a .ipsw's zip timestamp as a build date: it is the PACKAGING date and runs a few days late (1.2 was built 2002-07-24 and packaged 2002-07-31; 1.1 and 1.2.2 are off by one and four days). Some circulating copies are also modern repacks whose stamp is the repack -- the 1.0.2 copy says 2025, the 2.2.0.0 copy says 2023. The zip stamp is a fallback only, and anything outside 2001-2007 is discarded either way. HARDWARE BOUNDARY: 2nd-generation (touch wheel) support first appeared in family-1 firmware 1.2 (Apple's Firmware-1.1.2). Anything older -- 0.0, 0.2, 0.4 and 1.1 -- is 1G-ONLY, and the `generation` string is the only guidance the picker gives, so it must not claim 2G for those. 1.1 is the trap: it is a 2002 release with a modern-looking version number sitting on the wrong side of the line. scripts/extract_firmware.py derives the model list from the version rather than trusting a hand-typed one, so this rule is enforced at packaging time and not just documented here. LEGACY: the .ipsw assets remain on the release and are deliberately no longer referenced here; flashpod <= 0.1.7 ships a manifest that points at them, so deleting them would break those installs.
_models_comment: The iPod models flashpod can flash for, oldest first. `flashpod flash` asks which one you have and then offers only firmware whose `models` list includes it -- firmware is NOT interchangeable across models, and the 1G/2G split is the sharp one: 2G (touch wheel) support first appeared in family-1 firmware 1.2, so 0.0, 0.2, 0.4 and 1.1 are 1G-only and would leave a 2G unusable. Note that 1.1 is a 2002 image, so 'the 2001 ones are 1G-only' is NOT the rule -- the rule is 'older than 1.2'.
_models_tell: 1G and 2G look identical -- same case, same screen, same four buttons ringing the wheel. The only difference you can check is by hand: the 1G's scroll wheel physically TURNS (it is mechanical), the 2G's does not move at all (touch-sensitive). Since that pair is also the one where a wrong pick matters (0.0, 0.2, 0.4 and 1.1 are 1G-only), the labels lead with that tell rather than with the model name.
_max_data_comment: No firmware here caps the data partition below the 128 GiB LBA28 ceiling (that ceiling binds every one of these images; see --lba48). HARDWARE-TESTED 2026-07-17: firmware 1.0 (0.0) boots a 128 GB card AND plays audio whose clusters land past 14 GB, and 1.0.4 (0.4) boots a 128 GB card -- neither has a low ceiling, so no max_data_gb field is set. (An earlier 0.0 broken-folder that looked like a size limit was an UNINITIALIZED card -- 0.0 does not auto-create iPod_Control, so a flashed-but-not-init'd data partition shows the broken folder regardless of size; run init.) A max_data_gb field (decimal GB) on an entry would clamp its data partition; none is needed today. `flashpod flash --max-data-gb N` can still cap a partition manually.
_provenance_comment: Where these images came from, recorded because two of them are not obtainable from Apple or from any live download. 0.0 (Apple labelled it 1.0) is the LAUNCH firmware: recovered off a real iPod by the r/ipod community after a search spanning more than a decade (https://www.reddit.com/r/ipod/comments/pd9bqa/after_a_search_going_back_over_a_decade_by/), and that thread's download has since gone dead. Our copy was extracted from a Mac OS 9 1.0.4 firmware PATCHER that someone had rebuilt around the file -- which is also why the salvage repack below is needed: a patcher carries the image in Apple's distribution layout, not the on-card layout a 1G boot ROM can read. If this manifest ever has to be rebuilt, that patcher is the upstream, not an Apple download -- and it is no longer only a dead link: a copy is archived in this repo as 'iPod Software 1.0.0 Updater (Modified 1.0.4).zip', whose Info.plist reads '1.0, Copyright (c) 2001 Apple Computer' over a Mac OS Classic updater binary dated 2002-01-07. That upstream claim is no longer taken on trust either: running scripts/salvage_format0.py on the patcher's Firmware resource reproduces the shipped iPod_1.0.0 asset BYTE-FOR-BYTE, so the chain from patcher to release asset is now reproducible rather than remembered. ONE 1G VERSION IS STILL MISSING: 0.3 (Apple 1.0.3) has no image anywhere in the archive -- the sequence jumps 1.0.2 to 1.0.4. Its notes, recorded so a future find can be slotted straight in: 255-character filenames, adds Brazilian Portuguese, Danish, Finnish, Norwegian and Swedish. (0.2 was in the same position until its salvage repack landed; it is now a normal entry.)
_salvage_comment: The 0.0/0.2/0.4 .bin.gz assets are ver=2 REPACKS (see _provenance_comment for where they came from). The original 2001 distribution files carried their directory at 0x4000 with payloads 0x800 BELOW their absolute devOffset (a logical/mis-packed layout); written verbatim the 1G boot ROM read garbage and broken-foldered. flashpod re-lays the osos/aupd payloads into the hardware-proven format-2 container (dir 0x4000+0x4200, payloads sector-aligned at absolute devOffset from 0x4400), which the 1G boots. build_date/version are unchanged -- same firmware, bootable packaging. This is now scripts/salvage_format0.py rather than a hand edit, and it is verifiable: run it on the format-0 sources of 0.0 and 0.4 and it reproduces both shipped, hardware-confirmed assets BYTE-FOR-BYTE. Two details that only that comparison would have caught -- the u16 at 0x108 must be set to 0x010c (every genuine format-2 AND format-3 image has it; format-0 has 0x0000), and the install-state directory fixups are baked in, unlike every other asset, which ship as pristine Apple bytes and get fixed up at flash time instead. All three repacks are confirmed on real 1G hardware -- 0.0 and 0.4 on 2026-07-17, 0.2 on 2026-07-31 -- so the tool is validated at both ends: it reproduces two known-good images byte-for-byte, and the one image it produced that had no reference to match still boots.

firmwares.description: Last stock Apple-released firmware for 1G/2G iPods
Compatibility with iTunes 4.5 and the iTunes Music Store; improved playback performance
firmwares._note: Previously described as adding EQ presets, shuffle by album, track scrubbing, Contacts/Calendar/Clock and the CJK languages -- all of which are 1.1 and 1.2, inherited from when this list jumped 0.4 -> 1.4. Apple shipped this as 'iPod Update 2004-04-28', a single updater for every model made before that date, and split its notes by hardware. The two items above are the 'iPod without a Dock connector' list, which is what a 1G/2G is. DO NOT add the Apple Lossless Encoder from the other list: that was for dock-connector iPods and the mini only, and claiming it here would promise a codec this hardware never got. Incidentally the build_date below (2004-04-23) sitting five days before Apple's 2004-04-28 release is a small confirmation that the field means build, not release.

firmwares.description: Longer playback time on 1G (scroll-wheel) iPods; longer stand-by time on both. Apple listed these as the changes since 1.2, so they cover everything from 1.2.1 through 1.2.6 as well
firmwares._note: The last software for iPods without a dock connector. Apple's notes read word-for-word like 1.2.6's because they are headed 'Changes since 1.2' -- cumulative over 1.2.1, 1.2.2 and 1.2.6, the release that actually delivered the battery work. (An earlier guess here that 1.3 was the 3G-launch updater was wrong; 1.3 is the end of the pre-dock-connector line, not the start of the next one.) NO 1.3.1 ENTRY, on Apple's own authority: the 1.3.1 page says 'This updater installs iPod 1.3 software on your iPod', and the archive agrees -- the 1.3 and 1.3.1 images both unwrap to 009395f3…. 1.3.1 was an updater revision (Mac OS X 10.1.2 or newer, opening automatically from iTunes), not a firmware revision, which is why its changes were only ever documented as unknown. Apple's wording also confirms this entry's model list twice over: 'compatible with touch-wheel and scroll-wheel iPods without a dock connector', and 'install if you have an original or second-generation iPod ... with iPod software 1.2.6 or earlier'. Note that updaters are platform-specific but the firmware is not -- 1.3 shipped as a Mac OS 9 updater, a Mac OS X updater and a Windows/MusicMatch one, all installing this image.

firmwares.description: Longer playback time on 1G (scroll-wheel) iPods; longer stand-by time on both. The successor to 1.2.1 -- skip 1.2.2 unless you want its European volume cap
EUROPE ONLY -- permanently reduces the iPod's maximum sound output to meet European limits. Not the successor to 1.2.1; 1.2.6 is. Choose this only if you specifically want the volume cap
firmwares._note: The one entry here where a higher version number is NOT a better choice. Apple shipped this as a regional variant, so anyone scanning for the newest 1.2.x lands on a quietly volume-limited iPod. The description leads with EUROPE ONLY for that reason -- do not soften it.

firmwares.description: Battery icon now correctly indicates a full charge

Browse by album and genre; Calendar (iCalendar appointments and alarms); Clock; on-screen feedback showing when the FireWire cable is safe to unplug; Sound Check and Audible audiobooks with iTunes 3 on Mac OS X
firmwares._note: THE 2G BOUNDARY. The oldest firmware that runs on a 2G, and the build date corroborates it: 2002-07-31 is the 2G's launch month, so this is the firmware that shipped with the hardware. Everything older in this list is 1G-only.

firmwares.description: More than 20 EQ presets and per-song EQ set from iTunes; shuffle by album; track scrubbing from Now Playing; Contacts, holding up to 1000 vCards; Korean, Simplified Chinese and Traditional Chinese
Fixes compatibility with blue-and-white Power Macintosh G3 systems
firmwares._note: Was previously described as adding eight languages, 255-character filenames and the low-battery sleep-wake fix. Those are 0.2 (Italian, Dutch, Spanish; the sleep-wake fix) and 0.3 (255-character filenames; Brazilian Portuguese, Danish, Finnish, Norwegian, Swedish). The old text was correct as 'what you gain coming from 0.0', which is what it meant when 0.0 and 0.4 were the only 1G images listed -- but it reads as misattribution now.

firmwares.description: Fixes a rare failure to wake from sleep when the battery is low; adds Italian, Dutch and Spanish
firmwares._note: A ver=2 SALVAGE REPACK like 0.0 and 0.4, produced by scripts/salvage_format0.py from a format-0 33,554,432-byte full-partition dump (the 32 MiB of padding falls away with the re-lay; no separate trim). HARDWARE-TESTED 2026-07-31: flashed to a card and boots a real 1G. That matters more here than for the other two, because 0.2's source was a 32 MiB full-partition dump rather than a distribution file -- a different shape from the 0.0 and 0.4 sources -- so the re-lay had to find the payloads inside a padded image. It also confirms the layout independently of the byte-for-byte checks: the same code path, run on the format-0 sources of 0.0 and 0.4, reproduces both shipped images exactly. build_date is the image's own compiled-in __DATE__ string, 'Nov 28 2001', which lands between 0.0 (Nov 01) and 0.4 (Dec 23) as it should.

firmwares.description: Initial release for the original 1G iPod
Last stock Apple-released firmware for 4G grayscale. Apple shipped this as families 4 and 10 (two board revisions) but the firmware image is byte-identical, so one entry covers both
Last stock Apple-released firmware for iPod photo and the color-display revision. Apple shipped this as families 5 and 11 but the firmware image is byte-identical, so one entry covers both
